synopsis: Chapter 2 describes a 2019 collision at BHP’s Jimblebar mine in Western Australia: in bad weather, an unloaded autonomous truck lost traction and slid into a loaded autonomous truck’s path; their reported speeds were about 14 km/h and 27 km/h respectively [f1375, f1376]. BHP confirmed that speed-restriction procedures had not been applied, and WA DMIRS followed up on interim controls after the collision [f1377, f1378]. The booklet places the BHP incident within the Komatsu FrontRunner full-autonomy mining case, but Chapter 13 calls the BHP, Fortescue and Rio Tinto incidents unverified research leads worth checking before the real review, creating tension with Chapter 2’s detailed account [f1826, f11205, f11273]. Published requirement documents from BHP and the other listed miners were not found, leaving a gap in miner-specific acceptance requirements [f2599].
